reasons: The send route has no login or permission check, so anyone who can reach the backend can send mail through the server's Outlook.
The accuracy claim in the settings route is not backed by any test shown.

terms.meaning: A web address the backend listens on, together with the code that answers it.
A checked description of the data a request must contain.
Microsoft's email program. The server uses it to send mail.
Saving a query result as an Excel spreadsheet file.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and router setup
sections.what: Loads the web route tools, the Excel exporter, the Outlook sender, and the logger, and creates the router that holds these routes.
sections.why: Likely reason: standard setup for a route file.
sections.watch_out: If the Outlook helper needs a library that is missing, the whole backend may fail to start, not only the email feature.

sections.name: EmailRequest
sections.title: Email request format
sections.what: Describes what the email route expects: recipient, query, answer, sources, an optional subject, and whether to use HTML.
sections.why: Likely reason: checks the input before any email is sent.
sections.watch_out: The subject is typed as text but defaults to nothing, which a type checker would flag. Check this before relying on the subject default.

sections.name: export_to_excel
sections.title: Excel download route
sections.what: Writes the query result to a new Excel file in the exports folder and returns it as a download.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets users keep answers in a spreadsheet.
sections.watch_out: The file name uses the time to the second, so two exports in the same second may overwrite each other, and no file is ever removed.

sections.name: get_model_recommendations
sections.title: Model recommendations route
sections.what: Returns the preset model choices with their cost and descriptions.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the screen show advice to the user.
sections.watch_out: These are advice text only. The model the app really uses comes from the settings, so the two can disagree.

sections.name: get_optimal_settings
sections.title: Optimal settings route
sections.what: Returns a preset set of tuning values and says they are meant for 95 to 99 percent accuracy.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives users a reference when choosing settings.
sections.watch_out: The accuracy claim is not backed by any test or measurement in the code shown, so treat it as a claim, not a fact.

sections.name: send_email
sections.title: Send results by email route
sections.what: Sends the query answer and sources to a recipient through Outlook on the server, as formatted HTML or plain text, and reports success or failure.
sections.why: Likely reason: using the local Outlook avoids the need for a separate mail server.
sections.watch_out: There is no login or permission check, so anyone who can reach the backend can send email from the server's Outlook to any address.

summary: Provides web addresses for downloading query results as an Excel file, listing preset model and tuning options, and sending results by Outlook email.
purpose: Lets the frontend export answers and send them to people by email.
why: Likely reason: keeps export and email features apart from the main query routes.
how: The Excel route builds a timestamped file in the exports folder and returns it. The two preset routes return stored tables. The email route passes the request to the Outlook helper and reports success or failure.
inputs: A query result dictionary for the Excel route. An email request with recipient, query, answer, sources, optional subject, and an HTML choice for the email route.
outputs: An Excel file download, preset tables, or a success or error reply for email.
risks: The email route has no login or permission check and sends real mail. Exports are never cleaned up, and file names use the time to the second, so two exports in the same second may overwrite each other.
debug: Look for the Exporting query result and Sending email to log lines. Exports are written to the exports folder relative to where the program starts. If email fails, check that Outlook is installed and the Outlook helper is set up. Read the detail field of any 500 reply.
